result.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
result.summary: Long-horizon agentic tasks require a model to call tools over many steps at contexts of 100K tokens or more, yet many low-bit quantization methods are calibrated on short web text and judged on perplexity. This mismatch is costly: existing quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at or below 3 bits per weight match BF16 on shorter tasks like AIME, yet in published results solve at most 72% as many tasks as BF16 on DeepSWE, a long-horizon agentic benchmark. We propose NariQ, a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens generated by the BF16 model in agent sessions. On Qwen3.8-27B, NariQ at 3.0 and 2.5 bits per weight stays level with BF16 on two long-horizon agentic benchmarks, DeepSWE and Terminal Bench, as well as on AIME and RealWorldQA. Our checkpoint at 2.0 bits per weight trails this performance. To our knowledge, these are the first quantizations at or below 3 bits per weight shown to match their full-precision version on long-horizon agentic tasks. We release the files as Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF (https://huggingface.co/nari-labs/Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF), with inference available through our llama.cpp fork at https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 NariQ，一种基于 trellis 编码的训练后量化方法，用 BF16 模型在 agent 会话中生成的 token 做校准，使 Qwen3.8-27B 在 2.5–3.0 bit/weight 下于 DeepSWE、Terminal Bench 等长程 agent 任务上与全精度持平。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察是短文本校准与 perplexity 无法预测长程多步任务表现，且低位宽会侵蚀内部状态中任务必需的信息，可供核查低精度或压缩对 latent 状态保真度与长程评价指标的影响；但未涉及视觉证据或 latent 推理生成，关联仅为间接。
